title: Ruth 2
paragraphs: ¹ Now Naomi had a relative on her husband's side, a prominent and wealthy man from Elimelech's family, whose name was Boaz. ² Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go to the fields and pick up the leftover grain behind anyone who will allow me to do so." Naomi said to her, "Go ahead, my daughter." ³ So she went out, and began gleaning in the fields behind the harvesters. As it turned out, she found herself working in the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the family of Elimelech. ⁴ Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and greeted the harvesters, "The LORD be with you!" They answered, "The LORD bless you!" ⁵ Boaz asked the overseer of his harvesters, "Who does that young woman belong to?"

⁶ The overseer replied, "She is the Moabite woman who came back with Naomi from the country of Moab. ⁷ She asked, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' She came in the morning and has been working steadily, except for a short rest in the shelter." ⁸ So Boaz said to Ruth, "My daughter, listen to me. Don't go to glean in another field, and don't leave this one. Stay here close to my women workers. ⁹ Watch which fields they are harvesting and follow along after them. I have told the men not to lay a hand on you. And whenever you are thirsty, go drink from the water jars the men have filled." ¹⁰ At this, she bowed down with her face to the ground and asked him, "Why have I found such favor in your eyes that you notice me — a foreigner?"

¹¹ Boaz replied, "I have heard the full story of everything you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband's death — how you left your father and mother and your homeland and came to live with a people you did not know before. ¹² May the LORD repay you for what you have done. May you be richly rewarded by the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge." ¹³ She said, "May I continue to find favor in your eyes, my lord. You have put me at ease and spoken kindly to your servant, even though I am not one of your own servants." ¹⁴ At mealtime Boaz said to her, "Come over here and have some bread. Dip it in the vinegar." She sat down beside the harvesters, and he offered her some roasted grain. She ate until she was satisfied and had some left over. ¹⁵ As she got up to glean, Boaz instructed his men, "Let her glean even among the sheaves and do not rebuke her.

¹⁶ Also pull out some stalks from the bundles and leave them for her to pick up — and don't reprimand her." ¹⁷ So Ruth gleaned in the field until evening. When she threshed what she had gathered, it amounted to about an ephah of barley. ¹⁸ She carried it back to town, and her mother-in-law saw how much she had gathered. Ruth also brought out and gave her what she had saved from her meal. ¹⁹ Her mother-in-law asked her, "Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the man who took notice of you!" Then Ruth told her mother-in-law about the man she had worked with. "The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz," she said. ²⁰ Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "May the LORD bless him! He has not stopped showing his kindness to the living and to the dead." Then Naomi added, "That man is a close relative of ours — one of our guardian-redeemers."

²¹ Ruth the Moabite said, "He also told me, 'Stay close to my workers until they have finished harvesting all my grain.'" ²² Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It will be good for you, my daughter, to go with his women workers, so that you will not be harmed in another field." ²³ So Ruth stayed close to the women workers of Boaz and gleaned until the end of the barley and wheat harvests. And she lived with her mother-in-law.
